Prepare a Circuit for the Dipole Methods

Source: R/dp-circuit.R
dp_circuit.Rd

Builds and factors the circuit for a resistance surface once, so that several dipole-method runs on the same surface (different radii, source strengths, seeds or methods) can reuse it. Pass the result as the resistance argument of dp_omni(), dp_pairwise(), dp_flux() or dp_pathways().

Usage

dp_circuit(resistance, resistance_is = "resistances", flow_potential = TRUE)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances".

flow_potential

Logical. Also factor the uniform circuit (the same cells with conductance 1) that flow potential and normalized current use. Default TRUE. If FALSE, it is built when first needed.

Value

A dp_circuit object.

Details

The circuit is Circuitscape's default raster graph: every non-NA cell is a node, joined to its 8 neighbours by links of conductance \((c_u + c_v)/2\), divided by \(\sqrt{2}\) on diagonals. Cells with zero conductance (infinite resistance) are left out. A tiny conductance to ground (\(10^{-12}\) per cell) keeps the circuit solvable; the dipole methods inject balanced currents, so it carries essentially no current. Groups of cells with no links between them (separated by NA cells) are separate circuits, and no current passes between them.

The factorization lives in the Julia session. If Julia is restarted (e.g., by cs_setup() with more threads, or after a crash), the circuit is rebuilt automatically the next time it is used.

See also

dp_omni()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available()
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
circuit <- dp_circuit(resistance)
circuit
a <- dp_omni(circuit, radius = 10)
b <- dp_omni(circuit, radius = 20)
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
